records.title: Does ork reimplement slicer's roadmap editor or reuse slicer tui?
records.context: slicer has an editing TUI (slicer/docs/tui.md) that calls the same ops as the CLI. ork must edit roadmaps (PROJECT.md goal 2).

options.label: cli-editor
options.summary: ork's own editor over slicer CLI calls, consistent with the rest of the dashboard

options.label: open-slicer-tui
options.summary: ork suspends and opens slicer tui --root P for deep edits; ork does only reorder, start and park itself

options.label: both
options.summary: Common edits in ork, slicer tui on a key for the rest

recommendation.label: both
recommendation.reasoning: Keeps the common actions one keystroke away without rebuilding every slicer editor.

records.title: Does codex count as rate-limit-capable in v1?
records.context: vendor.ratelimit-detection is decided: classify only documented signals; anything unclassified stops the slice for the owner (adj show 23). The codex CLI help (codex --help and codex exec --help) documents no rate-limit or quota signal, and the spike forced none. A bad model gave an error item and turn.failed in JSONL (testdata/vendors/codex/04-bad-model.stdout); that is not a rate limit. So a codex rate limit cannot be classified in v1, and automatic fallback from codex is not yet supported by any documented signal.

options.label: stop-for-owner
options.summary: codex stays in fallback chains; a codex rate-limit exit stops the slice for the owner until a real capture is classified
options.tradeoffs: matches the decided rule with no new classifier; a codex limit costs an owner stop

options.label: no-fallback-from-codex
options.summary: codex is never a fallback source; a codex limit stops the slice, and codex may still be a fallback target
options.tradeoffs: narrower than stop-for-owner; still needs the same stop rule

options.label: read-docs-first
options.summary: look up codex's documented rate-limit signal in its online docs before v1, then decide
options.tradeoffs: delays the decision; the spike read only the local CLI help

recommendation.label: stop-for-owner
recommendation.reasoning: It follows the decided rule without a new classifier, and codex stays usable as a fallback target. The read-docs option may still add a documented signal later.
